newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner wins Russian oil deal - report.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner wins Russian oil deal - report.

text.p: Norway's Kvaerner ASA will sign in the next few weeks a 6.5 billion crown contract with U.S. oil company Exxon to build an oil and gas platform for Russia's offshore Sakhalin project, the daily financial Dagens Naeringsliv (DN) said on Wednesday.
Quoting sources in Exxon, DN said Kvaerner had beaten off bids from Brown & Root and Bechtel.
The contract is for a jack-up rig and deck for Exxon's Arkutun-Dagi field, east of Sakahlin Island, and also contains options for building other rigs, DN said.
The platform, which will have a production capacity of 110,000 barrels per day, is the first of five or six to be installed in the Sakhalin area in the next 10 to 15 years, the daily said.
A spokesman for Kvaerner said the company was hopeful of an announcement in the near future.
"But we definitely have not signed anything yet," he said.
